    "assembly_instructions": "1) Start from the FPGA PCB substrate (14x9 m floorplan) and overlay the silicon-die outline plate that bounds the placed-and-routed logic; on the -X edge seat the host interface: a PCIe x16 gold-finger edge connector feeding a host DMA/PCIe controller block, the boundary where coefficient vectors enter and transformed results leave. 2) Drive the controller into the forward-NTT input FIFO and natural-order output FIFO, then mount the eight interleaved BRAM banks along the left edge at 1.1 m pitch between them. 3) Drop the conflict-free crossbar network as a vertical spine just inboard of the banks, and place the inverse-NTT N^-1 scaling unit on its output side. 4) Build the open butterfly-array frame: lay a thin floor across the array, then bolt the two longitudinal steel rails and the mid cross-brace so the chassis stays open from above; populate the eight parallel radix-2 butterfly lanes (one per BRAM bank) by wiring each DSP modular multiplier into its symmetric modular adder (dark anodized) and subtractor (brushed steel), then both into the pipeline register; finally seat the four carbon-fiber radix-4 fusion yokes in the open gap between the multiplier and add/sub columns, each binding a lane-pair (0-1, 2-3, 4-5, 6-7) into one fused 4-input radix-4 butterfly unit so the eight radix-2 lanes reconfigure into four radix-4 BUs. 5) Place the shared modular-reduction stage to the right as two distinct members: first the cylindrical Barrett q-multiplier spanning all eight lanes, then the boxy shift/subtract+correction member abutting it, wired from every pipeline register. 6) Route the operand-return bus from the reduction member back over the array to the crossbar (grounded by a standoff post onto the reduction member), and route the operand-read bus from the crossbar east into the multiplier column (grounded by its own standoff onto the array frame), keeping the read, return and twiddle channels on three separate heights; cap each with a direction arrow so the read/twiddle/return dataflow triad is fully visible and the conflict-free read-modify-write loop is closed. 7) On the right, install the twiddle-factor ROM and route a brass broadcast feeder west to the elevated rail spanning the multiplier column (grounded by a standoff onto the array frame) so one fetched factor fans out to all eight multipliers; then add the address-generation unit, the radix-2/4 config selector, the schedule/FSM controller and the clock PLL. 8) For inspection, lift one fused radix-4 butterfly unit onto two riser posts into an exploded view above the array (three twiddle multipliers W1/W2/W3 -> constant j-rotator -> y0..y3 add/sub tree -> four-output register), offset toward the +Z half so it clears the central lanes in plan view, and clamp the ten-fin exploded aluminum heatsink high onto its riser stub well above the die so the datapath below stays visible.",
